title: Take-Home: Sample-Wise Double Descent
summary: A linear model's test error, plotted against the number of training samples n at a fixed model size, rises to a peak near the interpolation threshold and falls again on both sides. Reproduce the curve, explain the peak from the design matrix's singular values, and remove it with ridge.
rubric: Setup: the model class, the data generator with a known ground truth, the test error, and how n varies at a fixed model size
Curve: enough values of n on both sides of the interpolation threshold, and enough repeats that the peak is not noise
Explanation: why the error peaks near the threshold for this model class, and why it falls on both sides
Fix: a single change aimed at the peak, rerun on the identical experiment, with evidence the curve away from the peak barely moves
Deliverables: runnable code with its numbers, plus a short slide deck that a reviewer can follow without you, ending in what the fix cannot do
Questioning: which assumption your explanation leans on, what would break under different data or a different model, and the next experiment
